IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: high throttle rate + autoscale saturation on inference-worker-prod-3 (region-us-west). Throttle events spike, token/sec dropped 35%. Pager ID 2026-THR-9
Maya: I’m on it, joining calls. Paging @Jason and @Priya for capacity/traffic routing.
Jason: seeing elevated `throttle_ratio` on prod-3, path /v1/generate. Queue depth jumping ~12k -> 29k over 3m. Autoscale hitting max replicas.
Priya: confirmation from metrics: tokens/sec per replica fell ~40%, request latency up 2-3x for medium-length requests. Any customer-facing errors surfaced?
CS-Liz: CS reports a handful of enterprise customers seeing 5xx and increased timeouts in the last 10m. They’re asking for ETA and mitigation.
Maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase autoscale max for prod-3 (fast but costs) 2) route non-critical customers to fallback smaller model variant 3) enable temporary global throttling/backpressure for heavy clients. Which do we want first?
Tomas: we should increase max replicas by +20 for the pool (can do via console infra-ops). Will open a change and watch.
Jason: I’ll start a temporary route rule to divert non-SLA traffic to model-small (cpu-optimized). Patch in the router now.
Priya: adding a short-term alert silence for the noisy queue-depth alert so paging stops every 30s while we remediate. Set for 30m. Don't silence throttles entirely.
Maya: doing handoff: @Priya you own autoscale changes, @Jason you own routing, @Tomas you coordinate infra/TF if we need more long-term capacity. I’ll update CS and execs.
SRE-Responder: CHANGELOG: increased max_replicas from 120 -> 150 for inference-worker-prod-3 at 2026-06-12T21:05:23Z by Priya. No config drift.
Priya: change applied, watching metrics. Current queue depth trending down to ~9k after new replicas join.
Jason: router rule deployed: traffic tag `tier:non_sla` -> model-small. Initial effect: 18% of requests diverted. Latency on core routes improving.
CS-Liz: notified customers, giving rollback ETA and mitigation steps. No data exfiltration. Customers asked for follow-up postmortem.
Maya: quick check: do we think this is an autoscale config problem or workload change?
Jason: looks like a combination: a burst from a partner integration + our queue depth threshold too sensitive for this traffic pattern.
Tomas: right — autoscaler scales but provisioning lag + high KV cache warms caused transient saturation. We also saw throttle alerts fire before autoscale fully caught up.
Maya: action items for post-incident: (A) tune alert thresholds and add debounce/for windows, (B) add a new dashboard for tokens/sec per-replica + throttle_ratio heatmap, (C) update autoscale max and initial replica buffer for known high-burst partners, (D) add routing playbook.
Priya: propose concrete alert changes: current `queue_depth > 5000` for 1m -> change to `queue_depth > 8000` for 4m; add `throttle_ratio > 0.02` for 2m; introduce `tokens_per_sec_per_replica < 150` for 5m as an early warning. Also add labels for pool and model variant.
Jason: I like adding tokens/sec per replica. Also recommend we add an alert for `scale_lag_seconds > 30` to detect provisioning lag.
Maya: please draft Prometheus rule snippets for the oncall runbook.
Jason: dropping a snippet now:
```yaml
- alert: HighQueueDepthObserved
  expr: sum(queue_depth{pool="inference-worker-prod-3"}) > 8000
  for: 4m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Queue depth high on prod-3"
```
```yaml
- alert: ThrottleRatioHigh
  expr: sum(rate(throttle_events[5m])) / sum(rate(requests[5m])) > 0.02
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```
```yaml
- alert: TokensPerReplicaLow
  expr: avg by(replica)(rate(tokens_processed[5m])) < 150
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
```
Priya: we should make `ThottleRatioHigh` a ticket (no paging) initially, escalate to page if it's coupled with queue_depth or scale_lag. Avoid paging on noisy single-metric flips.
Maya: good. Also add an aggregated dashboard: left column per-pool tokens/sec, right column per-replica throttle_ratio heatmap, bottom row scale_lag and queue depth.
Tomas: I’ll create a Grafana dashboard stub and give edit rights to SRE and infra.
SRE-Responder: NOTE: created temporary silence for alert group `queue-depth-prod3` until 21:35 UTC.
Priya: current status: queue depth stable ~4.2k, throttle ratio trending down. Will keep autoscale max bumped for 1 hour then step down if stable.
Maya: CS updated and customers acknowledged mitigation. No SLA breaches confirmed yet but we’re tracking error rates.
Jason: reopening router to full traffic for a test subset, looks stable.
Maya: postmortem owners: Priya (autoscale tuning), Jason (routing/runbook), Tomas (dashboard+infra), Maya (incident write-up + exec summary). Please create PRs for alert changes and link them here.
CS-Liz: requesting a short customer-facing summary once postmortem ready.
Priya: creating PR for alert rule changes: will link -> https://git.internal/alerts/merge/4527 (draft).
Tomas: dashboard PR -> https://grafana.internal/d/merge/1289 (stub).
Maya: wrap-up: update runbook to include fallback routing earlier in sequence and recommended thresholds (queue_depth 8k 4m, throttle_ratio ticketing, tokens/sec early-warning). Follow-up sync tomorrow 9am PT to review and close action items. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Jason: great work team. 
Maya: ending handoff, leaving notes in incident doc. :white_check_mark:
SRE-Responder: INCIDENT CLOSED: 2026-06-12T21:33:43Z by Maya.
